questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Liechtenstein?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Liechtenstein article.

questions.proof: Its capital city is Vaduz, but its largest town is Schaan.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with Liechtenstein?

hints.nudge: Two countries are neighbours when you can walk from one into the other. Picture Liechtenstein on the globe and look at what it touches.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Geography” part of the Liechtenstein article.

questions.proof: Liechtenstein lies in the Alps, along the Rhine river, which forms almost all of its western border with Switzerland.

questions.prompt: Which language is an official language of Liechtenstein?

hints.nudge: An official language is the one used in schools, courts and government. The other three are spoken in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “People” part of the Liechtenstein article.

questions.proof: Most speak German, the official language, and many also speak a local dialect called Alemannic.

questions.prompt: What money is used in Liechtenstein?

hints.nudge: Money names often come from a country’s own words. The other three are spent in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “History” part of the Liechtenstein article.

questions.proof: After World War I, it formed a close partnership with Switzerland, adopting the Swiss franc as its currency.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “In 2003, voters gave the Prince more power in a referendum, and in _____ the country joined the Schengen Area, allowing passport-free travel with many other European countries.”

hints.nudge: It is a year in the twenty-first century.
hints.whereToLook: It is further down the Liechtenstein article, under the heading “History”.

questions.proof: In 2003, voters gave the Prince more power in a referendum, and in 2011 the country joined the Schengen Area, allowing passport-free travel with many other European countries.
